key_insight: PyraTok learns discrete video tokens at multiple spatiotemporal scales and aligns each scale with language, producing semantically structured latents that improve cross-modal alignment and zero‑shot transfer for video understanding and generation.
problem_solved: Existing video tokenizers use a single-scale codebook and weak language supervision, which yields coarse, poorly aligned tokens that limit text-to-video generation quality and zero-shot transfer across video tasks.
method: Build on a pretrained video VAE and introduce a pyramidal tokenizer that produces discrete latents at multiple spatiotemporal resolutions (fine → coarse).
Apply language alignment to each scale so codebooks encode semantically meaningful concepts tied to text, improving cross-modal correspondence.
Use the multi-scale tokens to condition reconstruction and generation, enabling scale-specific control and better zero-shot transfer for downstream video tasks.
impact: PyraTok provides richer, language-grounded video representations that improve text-to-video synthesis and zero-shot video understanding without task-specific retraining, making multimodal systems more flexible and generalizable for practitioners.
visual_elements: Pyramidal schematic: stacked feature maps showing fine-to-coarse token grids over video frames with arrows to text labels.
Pipeline diagram: pretrained video VAE → pyramidal tokenizer (multi-scale codebooks) → language alignment → generation/understanding.
Token overlay: example video frames with colored token assignments at different scales to show semantic grouping.
Before/after comparison: qualitative panels or small charts illustrating improved alignment and transfer (e.g., better caption match or retrieval rank—no absolute numbers needed).
paper_title: PyraTok: Language-Aligned Pyramidal Tokenizer for Video Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Adheesh Juvekar, Kiet A. Nguyen, Dong-Hwan Jang
